english: Let $P_1$ and $P_2$ be the planes $x+2y+2z-5=0$ and $2x+3y+6z+4=0$, respectively. For a real number $k$, let $\Pi_k$ denote the plane $(x+2y+2z-5)+k(2x+3y+6z+4)=0$. Let $k_0$ be the value of $k$ for which the plane $\Pi_k$ passes through the point $(3,8,-1)$. Then which of the following statements is TRUE?
(A) $k_0=-\dfrac{3}{7}$ and $\Pi_{k_0}$ bisects the obtuse angle between $P_1$ and $P_2$
(B) $k_0=-\dfrac{3}{7}$ and $\Pi_{k_0}$ bisects the acute angle between $P_1$ and $P_2$
(C) $k_0=\dfrac{3}{7}$ and $\Pi_{k_0}$ bisects the obtuse angle between $P_1$ and $P_2$
(D) $k_0=-\dfrac{3}{7}$ and $\Pi_{k_0}$ does not bisect any angle between $P_1$ and $P_2$
hindi: माना $P_1$ तथा $P_2$ क्रमशः समतल $x+2y+2z-5=0$ तथा $2x+3y+6z+4=0$ हैं। एक वास्तविक संख्या $k$ के लिए माना $\Pi_k$ समतल $(x+2y+2z-5)+k(2x+3y+6z+4)=0$ को निरूपित करता है। माना $k_0$, $k$ का वह मान है जिसके लिए समतल $\Pi_k$ बिन्दु $(3,8,-1)$ से होकर जाता है। तब निम्न में से कौन-सा कथन सत्य है?
(A) $k_0=-\dfrac{3}{7}$ तथा $\Pi_{k_0}$, $P_1$ तथा $P_2$ के बीच के अधिक कोण (obtuse angle) को समद्विभाजित करता है
(B) $k_0=-\dfrac{3}{7}$ तथा $\Pi_{k_0}$, $P_1$ तथा $P_2$ के बीच के न्यून कोण को समद्विभाजित करता है
(C) $k_0=\dfrac{3}{7}$ तथा $\Pi_{k_0}$, $P_1$ तथा $P_2$ के बीच के अधिक कोण को समद्विभाजित करता है
(D) $k_0=-\dfrac{3}{7}$ तथा $\Pi_{k_0}$, $P_1$ तथा $P_2$ के बीच के किसी भी कोण को समद्विभाजित नहीं करता
solution: $|\overrightarrow{n}_1|=3$, $|\overrightarrow{n}_2|=7$; $\Pi_{k_0}: P_1-\dfrac37P_2=0\iff\dfrac{P_1}{3}=\dfrac{P_2}{7}$, so every point of $\Pi_{k_0}$ is equidistant from $P_1$ and $P_2$: it is a bisector
solution_full: The planes $\Pi_k$ form the family of planes through the line of intersection of $P_1$ and $P_2$.

The normals $\overrightarrow{n}_1=(1,2,2)$, $\overrightarrow{n}_2=(2,3,6)$ have lengths $3$ and $7$. The bisector planes of $P_1$, $P_2$ are $\dfrac{x+2y+2z-5}{3}=\pm\dfrac{2x+3y+6z+4}{7}$, i.e. the members $k=\mp\dfrac37$ of the family.
So $\Pi_{k_0}$, which is $\dfrac{x+2y+2z-5}{3}=\dfrac{2x+3y+6z+4}{7}$, is one of the two bisector planes; option (D) is wrong, and option (C) has the wrong sign of $k_0$.

Which angle? With unit normals $\hat{n}_1=\dfrac{\overrightarrow{n}_1}{3}$, $\hat{n}_2=\dfrac{\overrightarrow{n}_2}{7}$: $\hat{n}_1\cdot\hat{n}_2=\dfrac{2+6+12}{21}=\dfrac{20}{21}$, so the acute angle $\theta$ between $P_1$, $P_2$ satisfies $\cos\theta=\dfrac{20}{21}$.

$\Pi_{k_0}$ is $\left(\hat{n}_1-\hat{n}_2\right)\cdot\overrightarrow{r}=\text{const}$; its normal is $\hat{n}_1-\hat{n}_2$, with $|\hat{n}_1-\hat{n}_2|^2=2-\dfrac{40}{21}=\dfrac{2}{21}$ and $\hat{n}_1\cdot(\hat{n}_1-\hat{n}_2)=1-\dfrac{20}{21}=\dfrac{1}{21}$.

Hence $\Pi_{k_0}$ makes the angle $\dfrac{\pi-\theta}{2}$ with each plane: it bisects the obtuse angle. (Equivalently, since $\overrightarrow{n}_1\cdot\overrightarrow{n}_2>0$, the member with normal $\hat{n}_1+\hat{n}_2$, i.e. $k=\dfrac37$, bisects the acute angle, so (B) is wrong.)
originality_note: New: the plane is picked out of the family through l by a point, and only then recognised as a bisector by its parameter (|k| = |n1|/|n2|), with the acute/obtuse decision made from unit normals (way 5). Closest known: the equation of the plane bisecting the acute angle between two given planes. Different because: the bisector is not asked for; it has to be identified inside the family from a point, and the type of angle decided.

concept_use.Plane bisecting the angle between two pl: Bisectors are P1/3 = +-P2/7; Pi_{k0} is the one with normal n1/3 - n2/7, and the angle it makes with P1 shows it bisects the obtuse angle.
concept_use.Family of planes: Pi_k = P1 + k P2 is the family through l; the point (3,8,-1) fixes k0 = -3/7, and the bisectors are the members k = -+3/7.

justification: Two ideas linked (family parameter from a point, bisector identification with the acute/obtuse decision) with a sign trap. Comparable with the planes-through-a-line work of 2026-P1-Q6 (L3) and the planes-containing-a-line matching 2023-P1-Q16 (L3).
